newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: South Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand pared intraday gains to end around two cents weaker on Thursday amid late offshore and local importer dollar demand as the market corrected after gaining ground for two consecutive days.
It ended the day at 4.5740/5790 on dollar from 4.5525/5575 at Wednesday's close after what dealers described as "reasonably active trade".
The rand started the day firm near its previous closing levels and maintained a 4.5500 to 4.5640 range during the day in good two-way flows.
In the afternoon session it edged weaker to end above 4.57 on local importer and offshore dollar demand.
Some traders felt a retracement was possible up to 4.59 but said the downtrend was not yet over and there could be a renewed strength to the 4.52 level.
"It looks like we will see further strength after this correction," one said, adding that the rand looked set to range-trade in a 4.52 to 4.62 band until year-end.
"The 4.6200/46250 level is looking tough to break on the topside...it should hold," the trader added.
Another senior forex trader also predicted the rand would steady out for the rest of the year with a top at 4.62.
Some noted that South Africa's decision to sever diplomatic ties with Taipei in favour of Beijing by the end of 1997 had created uncertainty and was seen as "a bit of a worry".
The rand was last trading at 7.6924/7054 on sterling from 7.6356/6485 on Wednesday. It was little changed at 0.3345/3350 marks from 0.3344/3349 marks previously.
Local bonds retraced to end back above 15.80 percent after nervous intraday trade, dealers said.
At 1418 GMT the key R150 bond was at 15.81 percent from 15.71 percent.
Yields ticked steadily higher as player started the day off long on stock following big moves on Wednesday which saw the yield on the R150 bond trade to a best level of 15.67 percent.
Bond dealers said the release of the headline third quarter GDP figure of 3.2 percent was slightly stronger than expected, but market reaction was muted.
The Central Statistical Service said gross domestic product (GDP) rose a seasonally adjusted and annualised 3.2 percent in the third quarter from a revised 3.7 percent second quarter rise.
But stripping out agriculture the core economy grew just 0.5 percent quarter on quarter, down from 1.8 percent in the second quarter.

"The market is likely to hold current levels...a cautious note has crept in and there are still underlying concerns about the high money market shortage and the long-term outlok for the rand," one trader a a major local bank said.
The next important economic indicators due out are October money supply and private credit extension figures at 1500 GMT on Friday.
The consensus forecast of 13 economists polled by Reuters was that private sector credit extension expanded 18.1 percent year-on-year in October, with the forecast range 17.7 to 18.6.
M3 money supply growth is forecast at 15.1 percent -- with a range 14.1 to 15.5 percent -- after September's 14.45 percent.

On the money market, banks quoted their three-month NCD rates higher at between 17.00 percent and 17.10 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also higher at between 16.40 and 16.65 percent from 16.30 and 16.60 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the shortage back above nine billion rand at 9.071 billion rand from 8.974 billion rand on Tuesday.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners bought a net 244.28 million rand worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying a net 17.20 million rand worth of bonds on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 9.81 billion rand on Wednesday from 5.86 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
